text: He says there are many types of diets, some based on restriction and others on frequent meals and snacks.
He also mentions calorie-counting approaches and criticizes the idea of treating the body simply as a machine that takes in fuel and burns calories.
He argues that obesity is not, by itself, the main disease but rather a symptom of a broader problem that he describes as poor nutrition and poor absorption.
He says people with obesity often have additional symptoms that, in his view, should be considered part of the same underlying problem.
He gives examples such as hair loss and peripheral-nerve symptoms including tingling, numbness, and tremor.
He also mentions fatty liver and says it is often treated as a common or routine finding.
He adds digestive problems such as reflux, heartburn, and irritable-bowel-type symptoms.
He argues that these symptoms are often treated as separate diseases even though, in his model, they fall under a broader problem of poor nutrition.
He says that by addressing what he considers poor nutrition and poor absorption, a person may improve overall health and reduce obesity.
He concludes that this approach can also help reduce excess body weight.
